plain: To step in between two sides and help them reach an agreement

webster.text: Middle; being between the two extremes.

more.text: Interposed; intervening; being between two objects.
Acting by means, or by an intervening cause or instrument.
To interpose between parties, as the equal friend of each; to act indifferently between contending parties, with a view to reconciliation; to intercede.

example.quote: The judicial power, in such case, could not mediate, or hold the balance between the two contending powers, because the legislative would undermine it.
example.cite: John Adams, Thoughts on Government, Applicable to the Present State of the American Colonies (Philadelphia 1776)
